what_its_for: This medicine is a type of botulinum toxin (a purified protein) given as an injection by your doctor. It is used to treat several conditions including: muscle stiffness or spasms in the arms, hands, legs, or feet (called spasticity) in adults and some children; abnormal head and neck movements or positions (cervical dystonia); uncontrolled blinking or eye spasms (blepharospasm); crossed eyes (strabismus) in adults; and excessive drooling (sialorrhea) in adults and children. It works by temporarily relaxing the muscles or glands where it is injected.
how_to_take: This medicine is ONLY given as an injection by a trained healthcare provider (such as a doctor or specialist) in a clinic or medical office. You will NOT give this injection to yourself at home. Your doctor will inject it directly into the affected muscle or gland. Each treatment session may involve one or more injections in different spots. The number of injections, the dose, and where it is given will depend on your condition. Do not try to change your dose or injection site on your own.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition, your weight (especially for children), and how you responded to previous treatments. Treatments are usually repeated every 3 to 6 months, but this varies by condition. It is very important to only use the dose your doctor prescribes. Never ask for extra injections between scheduled visits without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given in a clinic by your doctor, a missed dose means you have missed or rescheduled your appointment. If you miss your appointment, contact your doctor's office as soon as possible to reschedule. Do not try to double up on doses to make up for a missed appointment. Your doctor will advise you on the best time to reschedule.
storage: You do not need to store this medicine at home — your healthcare provider handles storage. For your information: the medicine must be kept refrigerated (36°F to 46°F or 2°C to 8°C) and protected from light. It must be prepared and used by trained medical staff. Do not attempt to obtain or store this medicine on your own.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor about ALL medicines you take, including vitamins and herbal supplements, before each treatment. Avoid other botulinum toxin products (such as Botox or Dysport) while using this medicine unless your doctor specifically approves them. Avoid activities that require steady muscle control or precise movements right after your injection until you know how the medicine affects you. If treated near the eye, avoid rubbing your eyes. If treated for drooling or swallowing muscles, be careful with eating and drinking. Avoid drinking alcohol excessively as it may increase dizziness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor RIGHT AWAY or go to the emergency room if you experience: difficulty swallowing, speaking, or breathing; weakness all over your body that spreads beyond the injection site; double vision or drooping eyelids that are severe; loss of bladder control; allergic reaction signs such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, dizziness, or trouble breathing. These may be signs that the toxin has spread beyond the injection site, which is a rare but serious condition. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve, if they get worse, or if you develop new symptoms between appointments.
when_it_works: Most people begin to notice improvement within 1 to 2 weeks after the injection. The full effect is usually seen by about 4 to 6 weeks. The effects are temporary and typically last around 3 to 6 months, after which your doctor may recommend another treatment. If you do not notice any improvement after 4 to 6 weeks, contact your doctor before seeking additional injections.
special_populations: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding — the safety of this medicine during pregnancy or breastfeeding is not fully known. For children: this medicine can be used in certain children for specific conditions (such as spasticity or drooling), but the dose is carefully calculated based on body weight. Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine and should be monitored closely. If you have a neuromuscular disease (such as ALS, myasthenia gravis, or Lambert-Eaton syndrome), tell your doctor before receiving this injection, as you may be at higher risk for serious side effects.
